/LILIAN

Baltic Exchange Market Report 28 August 2026
Baltic Dry Index: 3186 (79)
Baltic Capesize Index: 5336 (198)
Baltic Panamax Index: 2315 (23)
Baltic Supramax Index: 1647 (2)
Baltic Handysize Index: 881 (0)
CAPESIZE
The market ended the week on a positive note across the board, with the BCI 182 5TC climbing $6,294 from Monday’s $42,105 to close at $48,399. The Pacific finished firmly, supported by continued miner activity, with three C5 miners in the market and offers for West Australia/China initially indicated in the mid to upper $16s. A miner was heard fixed at $16.20, with a second fixture reported just below $16.00, while the C5 index ultimately settled at $16.180, up 0.635 on the day. The Atlantic also strengthened, with the C3 index increasing 0.959 to $38.364. South Brazil and West Africa business improved as bids gradually edged higher towards $37.50 against offers above $38.00, while a fresh C3 fixture was reported at $38.50 and subsequently repeated later in the day. All in all, the firmer fixture levels and continued cargo enquiry provided a positive tone into the weekend, with both basins ending the week on a noticeably stronger footing.
PANAMAX
As the week came to a close the market decided there had been enough activity already this week, and an upcoming holiday in the UK on Monday might have added to participants apathy. The P5TC average was up another $202 to close the week at $20,834, almost $2,000 above last weeks close. Sources said there was less appetite from Charterers to chase Owners inflated offers, whilst Owners saw no reason to reduce their ideas this week, so a natural end of week standoff ensued. Some brokers were hesitant to predict the next move in spite of the positive gains witnessed this week. A 82,000-dwt built 2013 was said to have fixed North China to India with urea at $15,000, but no further details emerged.
SUPRAMAX
The week ended with another small rise in the 11TC average which closed the week at $20,819, up $30, and only up $91 on last weeks close. The market has been searching for direction all week in mixed trading and a holiday in the UK on Monday did not help todays activity. Olam were said to have fixed an Ultramax for 62,000/10 grains New Orleans to ARAG for 9-15 September at $36.00 fio and the Nord Bay (64,228 2025) Jacksonville 1-3 September was said to fixed something on voyage basis, but it was not confirmed if they were linked. The Ultra OL (63,722 2025) New York 5 September went on subjects delivery Cape Henry for a trip Croatia intention coal at $31,000 with XO and the Armonia (58,609 2013) Barranquilla 29 August was also said to be on subjects basis South West Pass for a grains stem to the Mediterranean with Bunge, but the rate was elusive. The Delmax66 (66,565 2026) open Big Creek 2 September went on subjects delivery South West Pass trip Mediterannean with grains at $34,500, again with Bunge, and the Uma Naree (63,688 2020) Barranquilla 2 September went on subjects to ADM for a New Orleans grains stem to Atlantic Colombia, but there were no further details.
HANDYSIZE
The Handysize market closed the week on a notably quiet footing, with limited fresh enquiry and a generally cautious tone across most regions. Despite the subdued activity, the Baltic Handysize 7TC index edged up $6 to close at $15,855.

In Asia, a handy-sized vessel fixed a South China/Australia round voyage at $17,350, while increasing tonnage in the North Pacific weighed on sentiment. A 40,000 dwt vessel open in North Asia reportedly fixed for a WC India trip at rates in the $19,000s.

Elsewhere, the US Gulf remained firm, supported by healthy fundamentals, while market conditions in the Continent continued to soften.

Market Fundamentals
French Corn Crop Slumps to 15-Year Low

French corn conditions fell further last week, with only 28% rated good-to-excellent as of 24 August, the worst score since FranceAgriMer's records began in 2011, Reuters reports. Prolonged summer heat and dryness have hit the crop hardest of all cereals still in its growing cycle. The European Commission has already cut its 2026/27 EU corn production forecast by 1.8 Mt to a 19-year low of 50.1 Mt. With less domestic corn available for feed, domestic wheat is expected to be diverted to livestock use, squeezing EU wheat export availability, Argus reports. EU wheat exports climbed 1.8 Mt year-on-year to 13.9 Mt in 1h26, while corn shipments eased 0.4 Mt to 1.6 Mt, customs data show.

Trading Commentary
Cape
The Cape curve strengthened over the course of the day. September was the main focus, trading between 43,750–45,500. Early activity was concentrated around 44,500–44,850 before the market pushed higher through the afternoon, reaching 45,500 late in the session. October traded between 45,500–46,500, also firming through the day with repeated clips around 45,750–46,000 before reaching 46,500. Q4 26 traded between 43,500–44,500, with levels improving steadily into the afternoon. Q1 27 traded mainly between 29,750–30,000. Cal 27 printed at 33,200, while Cal 28 traded around 29,100–29,200.

PMX
The PMX market firmed through the session today. September was the main focus, trading in over 2000 lots between 21,650–22,100. Early activity was concentrated around 21,750–21,850 before the market pushed higher, with repeated trading around 22,000 and a late high of 22,100. October traded between 23,150–23,650, strengthening through the day and reaching the highs late in the session causing the oct v nov spread to trade 375. Q4 26 traded between 22,500–23,000, also moving steadily higher from the morning levels. Q1 27 traded mainly between 17,900–18,200, with stronger levels seen later in the day, Q1 v cal27 was paid at 50 Cal 27 traded between 17,950–18,225 and Cal 28 printed at 16,100.

SMX + HANDY
The SMX paper gained support, pushing higher. September was the main focus, trading between 19,750–19,900, with most activity concentrated around 19,750–19,850. October traded between 21,000–21,600, strengthening through the day peaking in the afternoon. Q4 26 traded between 20,400–21,000, with the market moving steadily higher into the close. Q1 27 traded between 15,700–15,900, also firming later in the session. Further out, Cal 27 traded between 16,000–16,100, while Cal 28 was active around 13,950–14,000 and Cal 29 saw a single print at 13,800.

The North Atlantic looked to an end user’s transatlantic tender after it was auctioned for a voyage from Narvik to Algeria over late September dates, though rates remain unconfirmed at this time.
